title: Six-round AES secret-key boomerang chain, s=2

target.description: Six standard 128-bit-block AES rounds with initial AddRoundKey and the last MixColumns omitted. Section 3.2 decomposes them into upper 2.5, middle 1.5 and final 2 rounds. The distinguisher does not use key-schedule relations.

setting.key_relation: One fixed unknown AES master key is used for all encryption and inverse queries; no related-key or chosen-key access.
setting.key_population: General single-secret-key AES keys; no weak-key restriction is imposed.
setting.plaintext_model: Initial one-diagonal plaintext structures followed by adaptively chosen friend pairs and inverse-diagonal exchanges of observed ciphertext pairs.
setting.reference_model: Distinguish the six-round keyed AES permutation and its inverse from a uniformly random 128-bit permutation and its inverse using oracle queries only.
assumptions: Adaptive access in both directions (ACPC in the source) is essential; these are not chosen-plaintext-only, known-key, or chosen-key results.
The paper estimates boomerang occurrence, friend-pair filtering and repeated-run success probabilistically; rounded analytical predictions are not full-scale reproduced measurements.
The construction uses the AES round transformations without exploiting master-key schedule relations; the six-round structural distinguisher applies to AES-128, AES-192 and AES-256.

time.note: Author-reported rounded equivalent number of AES encryptions (E), with oracle calls dominating the six-round construction; no independent normalization to S-box operations or wall-clock time is applied. D1 component accounting is unresolved; see coverage issue ytxq2025-first-boomerang-query-accounting.

data.note: Author-reported rounded ACPC block-query budget, summing chosen/adaptive plaintext encryptions and adaptive ciphertext decryptions; it is not a chosen-plaintext-only budget. D1 component accounting is unresolved; see coverage issue ytxq2025-first-boomerang-query-accounting.

memory.note: The endpoint has no explicit peak-memory budget. The 2^32-entry per-structure hash table in the pseudocode is not promoted to a whole-attack peak estimate.

preprocessing.note: No separate reusable preprocessing cost is reported. The paper's PC search over attack parameters is not priced as an attack setup resource.

success.description: Author-reported rounded Pr[output AES | oracle is six-round AES], not distinguishing advantage or the equal-prior average correct-decision probability. Section 4.2 uses Ps=1-[1-ps1*product(psm(ni))*ps2]^w and says the type-II error may be ignored by the Section 4.1 analysis; the rounded AES acceptance probability is retained without substituting a balanced accuracy.

evidence.locator: PDF p.4 / printed p.304 (native E and ACPC units); PDF pp.5,10 / printed pp.305,310 (AES key lengths and exact round boundary).
evidence.interpretation: The setting is single-secret-key encryption/decryption oracle access, not recovery or knowledge of the key. Grouping all three AES key lengths does not assert master-key recovery.

evidence.locator: PDF p.21 / printed p.321, Table 3 row s=2; PDF pp.20–23 / printed pp.320–323, Section 4.2 and Algorithm 3.
evidence.interpretation: boomerang-chain-s2-n-1-2-13-5-w2. The native parameter vector (n1,...,n4)=(1,2,13,5) uses s=2 middle boomerangs and w=2 repetitions. Time and data are the paper's rounded w*sum(Di).

evidence.locator: Complete exact primaryPDF1–29, all sections, displayed formulas/tables/algorithms, proofs and references.
evidence.interpretation: Full contribution inventory read; bounded forward checking and finite component validation are separately receipted. Full attack reproduction not attempted.
Local source obligation, not an assertion of attack failure or a replacement resource budget.

limitations: Targeted result paragraphs and tables were inspected; the full proofs and all references were not audited, and no author attack code was run.
Memory and separately reusable setup costs are not reported, so the existing all-coordinate Pareto comparator cannot certify domination or a frontier position.

The source's first-boomerang accounting remains an evidence task: Section 3.3 (PDF p.14) counts 2^70.84 initial chosen plaintexts and 2^74.42 adaptive ciphertexts, whereas Sections 4.1/4.2 (PDF pp.17,20) use D1=2^71.84+2^74.42≈2^74.64. Algorithm 3 (PDF p.23) again gives 2^38.84 structures of 2^32 blocks. The native endpoint is retained without silently correcting or resolving that possible counting-convention discrepancy.

field_conflicts.label: Connection-proof event overlap
field_conflicts.description: Theorem1/Appendix sums sufficient events indexed by swapped diagonal and column subset without an explicit disjointness/overlap correction. Two independent standard-AES middle-component witnesses satisfy multiple events simultaneously (t0 four events;t1 three). The additive proof needs an extra argument; this does not refute the numerical r lower bound or the complete attack.
